scope: Immutable v7 catalog (37 branches/18 rejected claims) plus scoped v8 evidence and two refuted claims. No new active branches.

branch_updates.evidence: T4.I: diagnosis physically passes n compulsory repairs; exact margin and expiry criterion; one-bit task encoder proved for one terminal decision.
branch_updates.remaining_gate: Two sequential tasks and maintenance: construct a readable sufficient interface without free history or designer posterior.
branch_updates.dead_end_trigger: Terminal sign code fails to preserve a later action or maintenance choice.
branch_updates.minimal_test: Two tasks with distinct action-loss tables; independent bounded-register controller enumeration.

branch_updates.evidence: Hidden selector health wears and is serviced with imperfect success; complete programs reserve worst-case actual command costs.
branch_updates.remaining_gate: Service policies across episodes and a priced fallback/guard circuit, not only one precommitted upkeep action.
branch_updates.dead_end_trigger: An advantage disappears when its trusted fallback or action-dependent resource trace is included.
branch_updates.minimal_test: Compare flip and fail-silent command drivers with an explicitly priced guard and recurrent selector states.

rejected_additions.claim: Flagged memory erasure only scales the value of any installed diagnostic apparatus.
rejected_additions.reason: With flip-prone command execution, the negative selector term persists even on erased messages; correct fallback requests can be inverted. The pure scaling law requires a reliable or fail-silent output contract.

rejected_additions.claim: At equal cost, preserving more diagnostic information is always preferable to maintaining its interpreter.
rejected_additions.reason: Exact v8 program enumeration finds selector service strictly better than perfect erasure protection at budget 6; their marginal benefits weight the task losses differently.

novelty: Classical Bayes/FSC/channel tools; no new general theorem established.
